title: The Amphitheatre and the Knot: Lacan, the Return to Freud, and Four Institutions
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Boulevard Beaumarchais to the rue de l'Odéon

stops.name: 95 boulevard Beaumarchais, Paris: the birth
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. The coordinate is the Nominatim geocode of number 95; a value of 48.8625/2.365 circulates and lands about 350 m off the boulevard, near the rue Oberkampf. The arrondissement is disputed, French Wikipedia giving the 3rd and OpenStreetMap the 11th, and is not adjudicated here
stops.campa: Jacques Marie Émile Lacan is born on the boulevard Beaumarchais, eldest child of Alfred Lacan and Émilie Baudry. The money in the house is trade: soap and oils on the father's side, and behind that the Dessaux vinegar and mustard works at Orléans, which belong to the grandfather's line and not to Alfred. The household is Catholic and observant, and the boy is raised inside that observance. Even the address is contested in the record, the French account putting number 95 in the third arrondissement and the map registers putting it in the eleventh.
suggested_refs: The birth register of the Paris arrondissement in which number 95 boulevard Beaumarchais fell in 1901
The Dessaux vinegar and mustard works of Orléans, the maternal-side family trade
sources: Elisabeth Roudinesco, Jacques Lacan: Esquisse d'une vie, histoire d'un système de pensée

stops.name: Collège Stanislas, rue Notre-Dame-des-Champs: the Catholic schooling
stops.date_confidence: the range 1907 to 1918 is attested by English Wikipedia; the month and day of entry are not recorded and are set to the start of a French school year. The coordinate is French Wikipedia's for the college, 48 deg 50 min 43 sec N, 2 deg 19 min 39 sec E; a value 230 m off circulates
stops.campa: He is sent at six to the Collège Stanislas, a strict Catholic secondary school in the sixth arrondissement, and stays eleven years, from 1907 to 1918. The discipline is religious and so is the instruction, and he will speak of both afterwards with a coldness that never quite becomes repudiation. The school's own roll of famous pupils, drawn up long after, does not include him. He leaves in the last year of the war, seventeen, with the Latin and the Greek and the catechism of a house that expected him to keep the faith.
suggested_refs: The Collège Stanislas de Paris, working entrances at 6 and 28 rue du Montparnasse
School registers for the classes of 1907 to 1918

stops.name: Faculté de Médecine, rue de l'École-de-Médecine: the enrolment
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year of entry; month and day defaulted. French Wikipedia gives the enrolment as running 1919 to 1932, and the internship and doctorate dates agree; summaries that close it in 1926 are unsupported. The coordinate falls within about 110 m of 12 rue de l'École-de-Médecine
stops.campa: Ruled unfit for military service, he enrols at the Paris Faculty of Medicine, the ordinary road into French psychiatry. He stays on its books thirteen years, through the internship at Sainte-Anne and up to the doctorate of November 1932. Summaries that close the enrolment in 1926 have nothing behind them; the French record runs it to 1932 and the internship dates agree. In these same years he reads philosophy on his own account, without a supervisor and without an examination.
suggested_refs: Matriculation registers of the Faculté de médecine de Paris, 1919

stops.name: Rue de l'Odéon: the reading of Ulysses
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The verified pool holds only that Lacan's documented avant-garde contact begins with Adrienne Monnier's circle in 1921 and names the Ulysses reading; the séance de lecture of 7 December 1921 is the event so identified, but no source consulted places Lacan in that room on that day. The pin is the corpus value for the rue de l'Odéon, inherited from the Joyce file, and stands for Monnier's shop at number 7 across the street. Claims that he was in Surrealist and Dadaist circles by 1920 are impossible: Breton's first manifesto is 1924
stops.campa: In the little bookshop of Adrienne Monnier, La Maison des Amis des Livres, Valery Larbaud reads passages of Ulysses aloud in French to a room of subscribers while the book itself is still unfinished and unprinted. James Joyce is present. So, by the one strand of testimony that survives, is a twenty-year-old medical student who has begun to circulate among the writers of the quarter. Fifty-four years later Lacan will open an international Joyce symposium at the Sorbonne. Whether he was in the room in 1921 cannot be established from anything reachable.
suggested_refs: La Maison des Amis des Livres, 7 rue de l'Odéon, Adrienne Monnier's shop
The séance de lecture of 7 December 1921, Valery Larbaud reading Ulysses in French translation

segments.name: Sainte-Anne and the Case of Aimée

stops.name: Hôpital Sainte-Anne, 1 rue Cabanis: the internship under Henri Claude
stops.date_confidence: attested for the internship period 1927 to 1931; month and day defaulted. The pin is the corpus value carried by the Artaud file. Two other Sainte-Anne pins circulate in the corpus, 48.8283/2.3391 in the Foucault and Breton files, and French Wikipedia gives the hospital as 48.8287/2.3385; the disagreement is recorded and not resolved
stops.campa: He enters the Clinique des maladies mentales et de l'encéphale at Sainte-Anne as an intern under Henri Claude. French psychiatry at this date works by description and classification, presenting the patient to a room and naming what is seen. He learns the method thoroughly before he begins taking it apart. The hospital is the ground he keeps returning to: the wards where he learns the trade, the amphitheatre where he will hold his seminar for ten years, the corridors he is finally shut out of.
suggested_refs: The Clinique des maladies mentales et de l'encéphale at Sainte-Anne under Henri Claude, 1927-1931

stops.name: Infirmerie spéciale of the Préfecture de Police, Île de la Cité: Clérambault
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1928-1929; month and day defaulted. The coordinate comes from the research pool without an independent geocode and is not corrected here
stops.campa: At the special infirmary of the police prefecture on the Île de la Cité, where the arrested insane of Paris are held for assessment, he trains under Gaëtan Gatian de Clérambault, theorist of mental automatism and of the erotomania that still carries his name in the textbooks. Clérambault teaches him to attend to what the patient does with language rather than to the diagnosis waiting to receive it. Lacan will later call him his only master in psychiatry.
suggested_refs: The Infirmerie spéciale près la Préfecture de Police, Paris
Clérambault's writings on mental automatism and the syndrome of passional delusions
sources: standard Lacan biography citing the Clérambault training

stops.name: Paris, near the rue Saint-Georges: Marguerite Pantaine strikes
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the attack. The theatre is named differently across accounts and no source consulted fixes the address; the pin is approximate and the arrondissement itself is soft
stops.campa: Marguerite Pantaine, a postal worker who writes novels nobody publishes, waits at a Paris theatre for the actress Huguette Duflos and stabs her. The precise theatre varies between accounts and no reachable source fixes the address; only the city and the day are firm. What Lacan finds in her is a text. The persecution is assembled out of the woman she wanted to be, and there is no lesion under it. She is committed to Sainte-Anne, where the intern who takes her case spends a year and a half on it and calls her Aimée.
suggested_refs: The case file of Marguerite Pantaine at Sainte-Anne, 1931-1932
Contemporary press accounts of the assault on Huguette Duflos
sources: Roudinesco, Jacques Lacan (on the Aimée case)

stops.name: Paris: the analysis with Rudolph Loewenstein
stops.date_confidence: attested for the period 1932 to 1938; month and day defaulted. No consulting-room address is identified in any source consulted, and the pin is the Paris centroid standing for an unlocated site
stops.campa: He begins his training analysis with Rudolph Loewenstein, a Polish-born member of the Paris society who will leave France for New York and help build the American ego psychology Lacan later spends his career attacking. No consulting room is named in any reachable source. The analysis runs six years, overlapping the thesis, the marriage and the entry into the society, and by Lacan's own account it is never brought to a proper end. He invokes that incompletion against orthodox technique for the rest of his life.
suggested_refs: Loewenstein's Paris practice, 1932-1938, and his emigration to New York

stops.name: Faculté de Médecine: the thesis on paranoid psychosis
stops.date_confidence: attested for November 1932; the day of the defence is not recorded and is defaulted. The surrealist reception of the thesis is reconstruction: the pool places Lacan's connections with Breton, Dalí and Crevel in the early 1930s but no source consulted dates their reading of the thesis itself
stops.campa: He defends De la psychose paranoïaque dans ses rapports avec la personnalité, built on the case of Aimée, arguing that the psychosis is not a defect of the brain but a structure of the personality, and legible as such. The medical faculty gives him the doctorate. The surrealists give him what the faculty cannot: Salvador Dalí writes to him, René Crevel and André Breton read the thesis as a document of their own programme, and he is taken up by a Paris with no interest in psychiatry at all. That crossing is reconstruction more than record.
suggested_refs: De la psychose paranoïaque dans ses rapports avec la personnalité, Paris 1932
Dalí's paranoiac-critical method and the Minotaure circle of the early 1930s

stops.name: École Pratique des Hautes Études: Kojève reads Hegel aloud
stops.date_confidence: attested for attendance beginning 1933 and for the seminar running to 1939; month and day defaulted. The chronology and geography lenses agree on 1933 as the start
stops.campa: For six years he sits in Alexandre Kojève's seminar on Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit, in a room that also holds Georges Bataille, Raymond Queneau and Maurice Merleau-Ponty. Kojève reads the master and the slave, and reads desire as desire for the desire of another, and a generation of French thought carries the lesson out of the building. Lacan takes the whole grammar: recognition, negation, a subject constituted by what it lacks. Hegel enters psychoanalysis through a Russian emigre's commentary and does not leave again.
suggested_refs: Kojève's Introduction à la lecture de Hegel, assembled from the 1933-1939 seminar by Raymond Queneau

stops.name: Mairie du 17e arrondissement, rue des Batignolles: marriage to Marie-Louise Blondin
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by French Wikipedia. The three births are attested to the month: Caroline January 1937, Thibaut August 1939, Sibylle November 1940. The date of the candidate membership within 1934 is not fixed
stops.campa: He marries Marie-Louise Blondin at the town hall of the seventeenth arrondissement. In the same year he is admitted a candidate member of the Société Psychanalytique de Paris, the French branch of Freud's movement, and begins the twenty-year membership he will end by walking out of it. Three children follow: Caroline in January 1937, Thibaut in August 1939, Sibylle in November 1940. When the marriage ends, and on what terms, the record does not say.
suggested_refs: Marriage register of the Mairie du 17e arrondissement, 29 January 1934
Membership rolls of the Société Psychanalytique de Paris, 1934

stops.name: Marienbad: the mirror stage, cut off
stops.date_confidence: attested for August 1936 at the fourteenth IPA congress; the day of the paper is not recorded and is defaulted. That Ernest Jones cut the lecture short rests on Lacan's own later account
stops.campa: At the fourteenth congress of the International Psychoanalytical Association he reads his first paper on the mirror phase: the infant before the glass, jubilant at an image whose wholeness it does not yet possess, and an ego founded on that misrecognition. Ernest Jones is in the chair and stops him before he finishes. He will take thirteen years to bring the paper back to a congress floor. No text of the Marienbad version survives and none was published.
suggested_refs: Proceedings of the 14th International Psychoanalytical Congress, Marienbad, August 1936

stops.name: Hôpital Sainte-Anne: the verdict on Antonin Artaud
stops.date_confidence: the date and pin are inherited exactly from the Artaud file, where the examination is dated 1938-04-01. Full membership of the SPP is attested to 1938 without a month; the two are placed in the same stop and the coincidence of season is not itself attested
stops.campa: Antonin Artaud is held in the secure ward, and the young Dr Lacan is brought to examine him. The verdict comes with the confidence of the new science: fixed, obsessed, finished, he will live to eighty and never write another line. Artaud has ahead of him Rodez, the electroshock, and the most violent decade of writing in the French language. In the same year the Société Psychanalytique de Paris raises Lacan to full membership, and he takes his place in the profession at thirty-seven.
suggested_refs: The Sainte-Anne case notes on Antonin Artaud, 1938
artaud.journey.json, the stop 'Sainte-Anne, Paris: Lacan pronounces'

stops.name: Paris: the society dissolves, the doctor is mobilized
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1940; month and day defaulted. No source consulted supplies a coordinate for the Val-de-Grâce service and the pin is the Paris centroid
stops.campa: The German occupation closes the Société Psychanalytique de Paris, and Lacan is mobilized as a military doctor at the Val-de-Grâce. The movement has been dissolved by circumstance and not by vote; the practice continues in private rooms, patient by patient, with no society standing behind any of it. He publishes almost nothing for the duration and keeps clear of the journals that go on appearing under the censorship. His third child, Sibylle, is born in November of that year.
suggested_refs: Hôpital militaire du Val-de-Grâce, Paris, wartime medical service

stops.name: 5 rue de Lille: the apartment, and a daughter under another name
stops.date_confidence: Judith's birth is attested to 1941 without a month. The move to 5 rue de Lille is tagged reconstruction in the pool and given variously as 1941 and 1942; the two are left standing. The coordinate is the Nominatim house-number geocode; values of 48.8592/2.3288 and 48.8595/2.3268 circulate and are street centroids
stops.campa: Judith is born to Lacan and Sylvia Bataille, who is still legally the wife of Georges Bataille and cannot divorce under the occupation. The child is registered under the Bataille name and carries it for years. Around this time Lacan takes the rooms at 5 rue de Lille that are at once his home and his consulting rooms until his death: forty years in one apartment while everything institutional around it is founded, split and dissolved. Whether the move falls in 1941 or 1942 no document settles.
suggested_refs: 5 rue de Lille, Paris 7e, apartment and consulting rooms 1941-1981, with its commemorative plaque

stops.name: England: five weeks among the military psychiatrists
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1945 and for a five-week duration; month and day are not recorded and are defaulted. The pin is central London standing for an itinerary of unnamed units; which hospitals he actually entered is reconstructed from secondary literature, not attested
stops.campa: He spends five weeks in England, where the war has turned military psychiatry into a laboratory: Wilfred Bion and John Rickman running leaderless groups, the group itself treated as the patient. He meets Ernest Jones, who nine years earlier had cut off his paper at Marienbad. He writes up the British experiment admiringly on his return, and then spends thirty years attacking the object-relations school that grows out of the same soil. Which hospitals he actually walked through is not recorded in what survives.
suggested_refs: Lacan, 'La psychiatrie anglaise et la guerre' (1947)
The Northfield experiments of Bion and Rickman

stops.name: Zurich: the mirror stage, delivered whole
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1949 at the Zurich IPA congress; month and day are not recorded and are defaulted. No venue is named in the sources consulted and the pin is the Zurich city centre
stops.campa: At the congress of the International Psychoanalytical Association he reads Le stade du miroir comme formateur de la fonction du Je, the mirror stage rebuilt and this time delivered to the end. This is the version that goes into Écrits seventeen years later, and into every translation made after that. It is no longer a phase a child passes through and leaves behind. It is a permanent structure: the subject held together by an image that is not it, the ego as the standing site of a misrecognition.
suggested_refs: 'Le stade du miroir comme formateur de la fonction du Je', Zurich 1949, as printed in Écrits

stops.name: La Prévôté, Guitrancourt: the country house
stops.date_confidence: the 1951 purchase is attested by Spanish Wikipedia; the French article on Guitrancourt dates his regular presence there from 1955 and the two are left standing side by side. Month and day defaulted. The coordinate is French Wikipedia's for the commune; values of 49.0667/1.7333 and 49.0333/1.7333 circulate and are 4 to 7 km off
stops.campa: He buys a manor in a village of the Yvelines, forty miles west of Paris, and keeps its old name, La Prévôté. Here he holds his books and the weekends that colleagues and students are summoned to rather than invited. The French account of the village dates his regular presence there from 1955 rather than 1951, and neither date is abandoned in favour of the other. Thirty years later he is buried in the communal cemetery a few hundred metres from the gate.
suggested_refs: La Prévôté, Guitrancourt, Yvelines, Lacan's country house 1951-1981

stops.name: Paris: marriage to Sylvia Bataille
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year 1953; no month, day or ceremony venue is recorded in the sources consulted, and the pin is the Paris centroid standing for an unidentified mairie
stops.campa: He marries Sylvia Bataille, an actress of Jean Renoir's films and the estranged wife of Georges Bataille, twelve years after the birth of their daughter. The occupation had made the divorce impossible, and the delay is that long. Judith is by then a girl of twelve, still carrying another man's surname. No ceremony venue appears in the sources consulted and the arrondissement is unknown. In the same year his own professional society moves against the way he conducts an analytic hour.
suggested_refs: The marriage record of Jacques Lacan and Sylvia Bataille, née Maklès, 1953

stops.name: Paris: elected in January, gone by June
stops.date_confidence: attested for the January election and the June resignation; the day of the resignation is not fixed and is defaulted. The pin is the Paris centroid: no address is given for the SFP's founding in the sources consulted
stops.campa: In January the Société Psychanalytique de Paris elects him president. In June he resigns, after a motion aimed at the analytic hour he keeps cutting short, the session ended at the moment a signifier arrives rather than at the moment the clock says. He walks out with Daniel Lagache, Françoise Dolto and others and founds the Société Française de Psychanalyse. It will spend ten years asking the International Psychoanalytical Association for recognition and will never receive it.
stops.quote: everyone is well aware what is meant by the deceptive phrase 'variable length'
stops.quote_source: critical commentary on the variable-length session, quoted in the English Wikipedia article 'Jacques Lacan'; the words are a critic's, not Lacan's
suggested_refs: The 1953 minutes of the Société Psychanalytique de Paris on training standards and session length
The founding of the Société Française de Psychanalyse, June 1953

stops.name: Istituto di Psicologia, Rome: the Function and Field of Speech
stops.date_confidence: tagged reconstruction in the pool: the date and venue are universally given in Lacan scholarship but the pool cites no primary attestation. The structuralist turn itself is dated by the Stanford Encyclopedia to the end of the 1940s and across the 1950s, not to a single 1953 moment
stops.campa: At the congress of Romance-language psychoanalysts he reads The Function and Field of Speech and Language in Psychoanalysis, and calls it a return to Freud. He is fifty-two and three months out of his own society. What he brings back is not Freud's biology but Freud's text read the way a linguist reads: Saussure's signifier, Jakobson's metaphor and metonymy, the kinship structures Claude Lévi-Strauss had published four years earlier. The unconscious is not a cellar of instincts, it is an order of speech.
suggested_refs: 'Fonction et champ de la parole et du langage en psychanalyse', the Discours de Rome, September 1953
Lévi-Strauss, Les structures élémentaires de la parenté (1949)

stops.name: Hôpital Sainte-Anne, amphithéâtre Magnan: the seminar opens
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year 1953 and for the Sainte-Anne period 1953-1963; the month is set to November, when the first seminar of the public series is conventionally placed, and the day is defaulted. The pin is the Artaud file's Sainte-Anne value, which disagrees with two others in circulation
stops.campa: Months out of the society, he opens his teaching to anyone who will come, in the Magnan amphitheatre of the hospital where he trained. It runs a year at a time, one subject a year, and it runs for twenty-seven years. Analysts come, then students, then philosophers, then people with no professional business there at all. In 1955 he gives a session to Edgar Allan Poe's Purloined Letter, reading a stolen document that everyone can see and nobody perceives.
stops.quote: The narration, in fact, doubles the drama with a commentary without which no mise en scene would be possible.
stops.quote_source: Jacques Lacan, 'Seminar on The Purloined Letter', delivered in this amphitheatre in 1955, translation hosted verbatim at lacan.com/purloined.htm
suggested_refs: The amphithéâtre Magnan at Sainte-Anne, seat of the seminar 1953-1963
Le Séminaire, livre I-X, the Sainte-Anne years

stops.name: Hôpital Sainte-Anne, amphithéâtre Magnan: Seminar V, the formations of the unconscious
stops.date_confidence: attested for the academic year 1957-58, the seminar Les formations de l'inconscient; month defaulted to November on the convention already used for the 1953 stop opening the seminar in this same amphitheatre, day not recorded
stops.campa: In the year he calls Les formations de l'inconscient he begins drawing a figure on the blackboard of the same amphitheatre: a horizontal line of signifiers running toward a meaning it cannot reach without first being read backward, crossed by a loop bent the other way. He calls it the graph and builds it a piece at a time across the sessions, giving psychoanalysis something no clinical vocabulary had offered it before, an algebra for what a sentence does to the person saying it before the sentence is finished. Three more years of teaching remain before the figure is complete.
suggested_refs: Le Séminaire, livre V: Les formations de l'inconscient, Sainte-Anne, 1957-1958
The graph of desire's earliest 'elementary cell' stage, introduced across this seminar year
sources: standard bibliography of Le Séminaire, livre V

stops.name: Abbaye de Royaumont: Subversion of the Subject and the Dialectic of Desire
stops.date_confidence: the colloquium is commonly dated 19-23 September 1960 in Lacan scholarship, organized by the philosopher Jean Wahl. This session's live sources confirm only the year: the English Wikipedia entry on the Graph of Desire states it was 'first proposed in a 1960 colloquium,' and French Wikipedia's Lacan chronology places a Royaumont colloquium in this same biographical period. The specific day range comes from the standard secondary bibliography and was not independently re-fetched this session; web search access was exhausted and several direct source fetches (nosubject.com, lacaninireland.com, lacan.com's chronology pages) failed or 404'd
stops.campa: At a colloquium in the abbey of Royaumont he delivers the finished graph as an essay, Subversion of the Subject and the Dialectic of Desire in the Freudian Unconscious. Four levels stand one above the other: the signifying chain crossed by the retroactive loop built three years earlier, the Other's reply folding through the mirror stage, demand overflowing into desire and the fantasy of what the Other wants, and at the top the drive circling an object it never reaches, jouissance fenced off by castration. The diagram draws not a mind but a debt, a subject made of what language asks before it can answer. Écrits prints it six years later.
suggested_refs: 'Subversion du sujet et dialectique du désir dans l'inconscient freudien', delivered at the Royaumont colloquium, 1960, printed in Écrits, 1966
The Abbaye de Royaumont, Asnières-sur-Oise, Val-d'Oise

stops.name: Tokyo: the first Japanese journey
stops.date_confidence: attested for April 1963 in the standard chronology of the travels; the day is not recorded and is defaulted. Sites visited beyond Tokyo are reconstructed. Lituraterre belongs to the second Japanese journey of 1971 and is regularly and wrongly attached to this one
stops.campa: He travels to Japan, lectures to Japanese analysts, and comes back with a thesis he will repeat: that a language written in two readings at once, the Chinese and the Japanese running inside the same character, produces a subject who does not repress in the European way and for whom analysis may be beside the point. He returns to Japan in 1971 and writes Lituraterre out of that second journey, not this one. What he saw beyond Tokyo in 1963 is not documented anywhere reachable.
suggested_refs: Lacan's 1963 and 1971 Japanese journeys
'Lituraterre', Littérature no. 3, 1971
sources: standard bibliography of Lacan's occasional texts

stops.name: Stockholm: the condition
stops.date_confidence: the 23rd IPA congress ran 28 July to 1 August 1963 and English Wikipedia dates the condition imposed on the SFP to August 1963; the geography lens gave July, which is preferred against. The day is defaulted
stops.campa: At the twenty-third congress of the International Psychoanalytical Association the price of the Société Française de Psychanalyse's affiliation is put in writing: the society may join, provided Lacan is struck from its list of training analysts. He is sixty-two. Ten years of negotiation between the two bodies come down to one name. The condition issues in the days around the congress and is known afterwards, in the French accounts, as the Stockholm directives.
suggested_refs: The Stockholm directives of the IPA, August 1963
Proceedings of the 23rd International Psychoanalytical Congress

stops.name: Paris: the society complies
stops.date_confidence: attested for November 1963; the day of the vote is not fixed and is defaulted. That he broke off the seminar in that month is attested; the exact session is not identified in the sources consulted
stops.campa: The society votes to accept the condition. Some of the colleagues who walked out of the old society beside him in 1953 are among those who vote for it, and the analysts he has trained are told their training does not count. He breaks off his seminar in November, mid-year and mid-argument, and does not finish it. He calls what has been done to him an excommunication and goes on calling it that for eighteen years. Within eight weeks he is teaching again, in a building the profession does not control.
suggested_refs: The November 1963 vote of the Société Française de Psychanalyse
Seminar X, L'angoisse, and the seminar broken off in November 1963

stops.name: École Normale Supérieure, salle Dussane: the seminar reopens
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the reopening of the seminar at the rue d'Ulm. The pin is the corpus value for 45 rue d'Ulm, inherited from the Foucault file; a value of 48.842/2.3459 circulates in the research pool. Which philosophers sat in which year is attested only loosely
stops.campa: Louis Althusser gives him a room at the École Normale Supérieure, and the seminar reopens in the salle Dussane before an audience no longer chiefly medical. Michel Foucault, Gilles Deleuze, Luce Irigaray and Julia Kristeva sit in it at one time or another. He opens with The Four Fundamental Concepts of Psychoanalysis and begins by asking whether psychoanalysis is a science, five weeks after being told he may not teach it. Claude Lévi-Strauss had backed the move onto the premises.
stops.quote: In order to understand the Freudian concepts, one must set out on the basis that it is the subject who is called.
stops.quote_source: attributed to The Four Fundamental Concepts of Psycho-Analysis, trans. Alan Sheridan (Norton, 1978), retrieved through a secondary aggregator whose neighbouring entries showed transcription corruption; tagged reconstruction and not confirmed against the Sheridan text
suggested_refs: Le Séminaire, livre XI: Les quatre concepts fondamentaux de la psychanalyse, rue d'Ulm, 1964
The salle Dussane, École Normale Supérieure, 45 rue d'Ulm

stops.name: Paris: the founding act of the École Freudienne
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the Acte de fondation. No address is given for the school's founding in the sources consulted and the pin is the Paris centroid
stops.campa: He signs an Acte de fondation and creates the École Freudienne de Paris. He founds it as a place where his teaching cannot be voted on by a foreign body. The school is built with three sections, pure psychoanalysis, applied psychoanalysis, and an inventory of the Freudian field, and it admits members who are not analysts and never will be. Half the assets of the broken Société Française de Psychanalyse follow him into it. He will dissolve it himself in 1980.
suggested_refs: The Acte de fondation of the École Freudienne de Paris, 21 June 1964

stops.name: La Prévôté, Guitrancourt: the student who will edit everything
stops.date_confidence: the pool's 1963 date is corrected to 1964: English Wikipedia's article on Jacques-Alain Miller places his first stay at La Prévôté, to read the seminar transcriptions, after the summer of 1964. The month is inferred from that summer and the day defaulted
stops.campa: Jacques-Alain Miller, a philosophy student of Althusser's at the rue d'Ulm, comes out to La Prévôté to read the transcriptions of the seminar. He meets Judith Lacan there. They marry in 1966; he compiles the index of concepts for Écrits in the same year, and from 1973 he transcribes and edits the seminar itself, volume after volume, for the next fifty years. Whether the meeting falls in 1963 or 1964 is disputed, and the later year is the one the record supports.
suggested_refs: Miller's stays at La Prévôté, Guitrancourt, from 1964
The marriage of Jacques-Alain Miller and Judith Lacan, 1966

stops.name: Éditions du Seuil, rue Jacob: Écrits
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1966; month and day defaulted. The two-volume reissue is 1970 and 1971 in the Points edition, not 1969 as circulates, and not 1969-1971

stops.name: Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore: the structuralist controversy
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day-range: the colloquium runs 18 to 21 October 1966. The pin is inherited byte-identical from the Barthes and Deleuze files
stops.campa: The colloquium called The Languages of Criticism and the Sciences of Man convenes to introduce French thought to the American university. Lacan speaks in English, on structure as the inmixing of an otherness prerequisite to any subject whatever. Jacques Derrida reads a paper that dismantles structuralism while the audience is still learning the word. Twenty-eight years earlier this same speaker had stood in a ward at Sainte-Anne and told Antonin Artaud he would never write again. The proceedings, reprinted as The Structuralist Controversy, will name the moment for American readers.
stops.quote: the unconscious is structured as a language
stops.quote_source: Jacques Lacan, 'Of Structure as the Inmixing of an Otherness Prerequisite to Any Subject Whatever', in The Structuralist Controversy, ed. Macksey and Donato (Johns Hopkins Press, 1970); text at lacan.com/hotel.htm

stops.name: Paris: the Pass
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1967; month and day defaulted. No address is recorded and the pin is the Paris centroid standing for the École Freudienne
stops.campa: He institutes la passe. A candidate who believes he has become an analyst tells two passeurs, themselves in analysis, what happened in his; the passeurs carry the account, without him, to a jury that decides. Nothing is written down and the candidate is never in the room where the verdict is reached. It is a procedure for transmitting what the school itself calls untransmissible, and it divides the membership for as long as the membership exists. He never revokes it. What exactly the jury is certifying, the school never settles.
stops.quote: What could be more convincing, moreover, than the gesture of laying one's cards face up on the table?
stops.quote_source: Jacques Lacan, 'Seminar on The Purloined Letter' (1955), on Dupin's apparent transparency of method; lacan.com/purloined.htm. The line is not from the texts on the Pass and is placed here for its subject, not its provenance
suggested_refs: The Proposition of 9 October 1967 on the psychoanalyst of the School

stops.campa: He goes out to the experimental university built in the Bois de Vincennes for the students that May 1968 produced, and is heckled from the floor. The buildings themselves are pulled down in 1980.

stops.name: Università degli Studi di Milano: the psychoanalytic discourse
stops.date_confidence: attested for May 1972; the day is not recorded and is defaulted. Anti-Oedipus is attested to 1972 without a month, and the coincidence of season with the Milan lecture is not itself attested
stops.campa: He lectures at the university of Milan on the psychoanalytic discourse, one of several forays that carry the teaching out of France while the institution around it hardens. In Paris the same year, Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari publish Anti-Oedipus. Guattari had been Lacan's analysand. stops.name: Éditions du Seuil: the seminar becomes a book
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1973 as the start of Miller's formal transcription and editing; month and day defaulted
stops.campa: Miller begins to establish the seminar as a text. He starts with the eleventh year, The Four Fundamental Concepts of Psychoanalysis, delivered at the rue d'Ulm nine years earlier, and works from stenographic transcripts into readable French that Lacan approves. Lacan signs off on the method and never writes the books himself. Every volume carries his name on the cover and his son-in-law's decisions inside it, sentence by sentence, and no rival version of the teaching exists to be set against it. Volumes are still appearing forty years after his death.

stops.name: The Sorbonne: Joyce le symptôme
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day in the standard bibliography for the opening lecture of the 5th International James Joyce Symposium. The Seminar XXIII date of 1975-76 is attested for the year of delivery
stops.campa: He opens the fifth International James Joyce Symposium with a lecture called Joyce le symptôme, prepared with the Joyce scholar Jacques Aubert. Reading Finnegans Wake, he argues that Joyce made of his writing a fourth ring holding the other three together where the paternal function had failed: not a symptom to be cured but a sinthome, a knot deliberately tied. That winter's seminar takes the word for its title. Fifty-four years earlier, if one account holds, he had heard Ulysses read aloud in a bookshop before it was a book.

stops.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge: the last stop
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day in the standard chronology of the 1975 trip. The characterization of the MIT audience is reconstruction and is not attested in the sources consulted
stops.campa: He speaks at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, the last stop of the American circuit, in a place where the word structure carries an engineering sense rather than a Freudian one. The remarks from the whole trip are gathered afterwards among the conferences and interventions in North American universities. Nothing in the tour alters his teaching and nothing in it alters American psychoanalysis. What it alters is which departments in the United States will be reading him ten years later.
stops.quote: To explain art by the symptom seems more serious to me.
stops.quote_source: Lacan, United States lecture series, November-December 1975, as recorded on lacan.com/itinerary.htm
suggested_refs: 'Conférences et entretiens dans des universités nord-américaines', Scilicet 6/7

stops.name: Paris: the school is dissolved
stops.date_confidence: attested for January 1980; French sources date the opening of the dissolution to 5 January 1980. No address is recorded and the pin is the Paris centroid
stops.campa: He dissolves the École Freudienne de Paris. The school has become, he says, the kind of institution that manufactures orthodoxy, and it is dissolved to keep the teaching from setting hard. He is seventy-eight and increasingly ill; it is the third institutional rupture of his working life, and the first he has caused. More than twenty splinter groups come out of the wreck within the decade, each claiming the transmission and none conceding it to another. Members learn of it by letter.
suggested_refs: Lettre de dissolution, 5 January 1980
The successor groups of the dissolved École Freudienne de Paris

stops.name: Paris: la Cause freudienne
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by French Wikipedia. The pool dated this founding to 1981, conflating it with the École de la Cause freudienne constituted the following year; the correction is applied and the two bodies are kept apart
stops.campa: Six weeks after the dissolution he announces la Cause freudienne and puts its direction in the hands of Solange Faladé, Charles Melman and Jacques-Alain Miller. It is not the École de la Cause freudienne, which is constituted the following year and which Miller will run. The two bodies are routinely collapsed into one another, and the collapse costs a year of the record. Whether the new body was meant to inherit the school or to replace it is not settled by the announcement itself.
suggested_refs: The founding of la Cause freudienne, 21 February 1980
The École de la Cause freudienne, constituted 1981

stops.name: Caracas: the first meeting of the Freudian Field
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the founding of the Institut du Champ freudien at Caracas and for the address itself, which is the last public one of his life. The Caracas Discourse is quoted across the secondary literature without a single agreed printed text
stops.campa: He crosses the Atlantic for the first meeting of the Freudian Field, called at Caracas because the teaching has taken root in Spanish America more deeply than anywhere outside France. Analysts come from Argentina, Venezuela and Spain to found the Institut du Champ freudien in his name. It is the last public address of his life, and no agreed printed text of it exists anywhere in the literature that quotes it. He tells them it is up to them to be Lacanians if they wish, and that he is a Freudian.
stops.quote: It is up to you to be Lacanians if you wish; I am a Freudian.
stops.quote_source: the Caracas Discourse, First Meeting of the Freudian Field, 12 July 1980, quoted across the Lacanian secondary literature
suggested_refs: The Caracas Discourse, 12 July 1980
The Institut du Champ freudien
sources: Lacanian secondary literature on the Caracas Discourse

stops.name: Paris, 6th arrondissement: the death
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day. French Wikipedia specifies the 6th arrondissement without naming a clinic or an address; accounts differ on whether he died at home or in hospital and the difference is not resolved. A generic Paris centroid of 48.8566/2.3522 circulates for this event and contradicts the arrondissement
stops.campa: He dies in the sixth arrondissement of Paris, eighty years old. He has outlived the society he joined in 1934, the society he founded in 1953, and the school he founded in 1964 and dissolved in 1980. The seminar had stopped the year before that. Whether the death comes at home or in a clinic is not settled: the French record fixes the arrondissement and the day, names no clinic and no street, and goes no further. A generic Paris centroid circulates for the event and contradicts the arrondissement.
suggested_refs: Death record, 6th arrondissement of Paris, 9 September 1981

stops.name: Cimetière de Guitrancourt: the village grave
stops.date_confidence: the month of the burial is attested; the day is not, and is set after the 9 September death rather than taken from any source. Burial in the communal cemetery is confirmed by the French article on Guitrancourt. Two wrong coordinates for the village circulate, 49.0667/1.7333 and 49.0333/1.7333
stops.campa: He is buried in the communal cemetery of Guitrancourt, a village of a few hundred people, beside the house he had kept for thirty years. There is no Paris necropolis, no monument, no procession of the schools. The grave is a slab in a country churchyard within sight of the fields. A plaque goes up later at 5 rue de Lille, on the building where he had lived and received patients for forty years. The month of the burial is recorded and the day is not.
suggested_refs: The communal cemetery of Guitrancourt, Yvelines
The commemorative plaque at 5 rue de Lille, Paris 7e

stops.name: Éditions du Seuil: the complete English Écrits
stops.date_confidence: attested for 2006 as the year of the complete Fink translation; month and day defaulted. The partial Sheridan translation is 1977. Le Monde's list of the hundred books of the century is attested without a date in the sources consulted
stops.campa: The seminar goes on being published without him, volume by volume, Miller transcribing and Seuil printing, into the 2010s and past them. Le Monde puts Écrits on its list of the hundred books of the century. The complete English translation does not exist until Bruce Fink finishes it in 2006, forty years after the French and twenty-five after the death, so that for a quarter of a century the Anglophone argument about the book was conducted over a third of it. The two-volume reissue of 1970 and 1971 is still routinely misdated to 1969.
